# Working with Spatial Data in R - Vector Data

## Highlights

- Vector data represent spatial features as **geometries**: points, lines, and polygons.
  - *Point* = single coordinate pair
  - *Line* = sequence of coordinate pairs
  - *Polygon* = sequence of coordinate pairs, with the last overlapping the first.
- Geometries are stored as coordinate pairs in their own column in a **spatial dataframe**.
- Geometries and spatial dataframes are also associated with a **coordinate reference system** (crs)
  - The crs defines origin and axes to which the coordinate pairs are referenced.
  - A crs can be geographic and use angular units (e.g. latitude/longitude) ;\
    Or it can be projected and use linear units (e.g. UTM, State Plane)

```{r setup}
#Import packages
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(fs)
library(sf)
library(mapview)

#Set mapview basemaps
mapview::mapviewOptions(basemaps = c("OpenStreetMap","Esri.WorldImagery"))

#Local Paths
raw_folder = here('Data/raw')
processed_folder = here('Data/processed')

#Box drive path
current_os <- Sys.info()[["sysname"]]
if (current_os == "Darwin") {
  box_path = fs::path_home("Library","CloudStorage","Box-Box")
} else if (current_os == "Windows") {
  box_path = fs::path_home("Box")
} else if (current_os == "Linux") {
  print("Running on Linux; Box drive is not supported")
}
```


## Creating a spatial feature class from a table
A table with coordinate information can be read into a spatial dataframe using the st `st_as_sf` function. In this example, we read in the `NWIS_SiteInfo_NE_RAW.csv` file, which has an "x" (`dec_long_va`) and a "y" (`dec_lat_va`) column, in as a spatial dataframe. 

```{r table to spatial df}
#First read in the file as a dataframe
NWIS_filename <- here(raw_folder,'NWIS_SiteInfo_NE_RAW.csv')
NWIS_df <- read.csv(NWIS_filename)

#Then convert to a spatial dataframe using `st_as_sf`, 
# specifying the coordinate fields and the crs
NWIS_sdf <- st_as_sf(
  x = NWIS_df, 
  coords = c('dec_long_va','dec_lat_va'),
  crs = 4326
)

#View the dataframe with MapView
mapview(NWIS_sdf)

```


## Spatial Operations

### Spatial Join

- A spatial join assigns values in one dataset based on its overlap with a second spatial dataset. For example, if we wanted to tag each of our NWIS points with the county in which it falls, we would *spatially join* the county data to the points. 
  - Note here, we are reading county data in as a GeoJSON hosted here <https://eric.clst.org/tech/usgeojson/>

```{r spatial join}
# Read in the county feature class
counties_filename <- here(raw_folder,'ne_10m_admin_2_counties.zip')
counties_url <- 'https://eric.clst.org/assets/wiki/uploads/Stuff/gz_2010_us_050_00_5m.json'
counties_sdf <- st_read(counties_url)
```
